title: Acciones en curso
description: Presente continuo, pasado continuo, y cuándo usarlos frente al presente/pasado simple.

grammarTopics.title: Presente continuo
grammarTopics.explanationEs: Se usa para lo que está pasando ahora o alrededor de este momento. Forma: am/is/are + verbo-ing. 'I'm working now', 'They aren't listening'. Se diferencia del presente simple (rutinas) en que describe la acción en progreso.

grammarTopics.title: Pasado continuo
grammarTopics.explanationEs: Se usa para acciones en progreso en un momento del pasado. Forma: was/were + verbo-ing. 'I was reading when you arrived'. Suele aparecer como marco de una acción en pasado simple que la interrumpe.

grammarTopics.title: Verbos de estado
grammarTopics.explanationEs: Verbos como know, want, like, believe, need o understand describen estados, no acciones. Normalmente NO se usan en continuo: se dice 'I know the answer', no 'I am knowing the answer'.

payload.explanation: Presente continuo con 'it' (3ª persona singular): is + verbo-ing → 'it is raining'.
Con 'they' (plural) usamos 'are' + verbo-ing: 'they are working'.
Presente continuo con 'I': 'I am reading' o su contracción 'I'm reading'.
Negativo: is + not + verbo-ing → 'isn't watching' o 'is not watching'.
Pregunta en presente continuo: palabra Wh + verbo auxiliar (are) + sujeto + verbo-ing: 'Why are you smiling now?'
'Listen!' señala que la acción ocurre en este momento → presente continuo: 'is crying'.
Presente continuo con 'we': 'We are learning' o contraído 'We're learning'.
La pregunta 'What are you doing?' pide una respuesta en presente continuo: 'I'm cooking dinner.'

payload.prompt: I ___ TV when the phone rang.
payload.explanation: Pasado continuo para la acción en curso ('was watching') interrumpida por otra en pasado simple ('rang').
Acción en progreso en un momento pasado (a las 8) → pasado continuo: 'were having'.
'While + pasado continuo' presenta la acción larga: 'While she was walking home...'.
Pregunta en pasado continuo: Wh + were + sujeto + verbo-ing: 'What were you doing at ten?'

payload.prompt: We ___ football when it started to snow.
payload.explanation: La acción larga interrumpida va en pasado continuo: 'were playing'.
En pasado continuo: I/he/she/it → was; you/we/they → were.

acceptable: I was reading when you arrived.
I was reading when you came.
I was reading when you got here.
payload.explanation: Pasado continuo (was reading) + pasado simple (arrived/came) para la interrupción.

payload.audioText: At six o'clock we were having dinner and watching a movie.

sub.prompt: What were they doing at six?
options: They were having dinner and watching a movie.
They had dinner and went to the cinema.
They are having dinner and watching a movie.

payload.explanation: El audio dice 'we were having dinner and watching a movie' — dos acciones en progreso a las seis.

payload.prompt: I usually ___ coffee, but today I'm drinking tea.
payload.explanation: 'usually' señala rutina → presente simple ('drink'). El contraste con 'today I'm drinking' marca la excepción de hoy.
'Look!' + acción justo en este momento → presente continuo: 'is raining'.
'know' es un verbo de estado: no se usa en continuo. Se dice 'I know', nunca 'I am knowing'.
'usually' → rutina en presente simple ('drives'). 'today' + acción hoy → presente continuo ('is taking').
Adverbio de frecuencia ('often') antes del verbo principal en presente simple: 'She often works from home'.
La pregunta '¿Estás ocupado?' se responde con lo que estás haciendo ahora → presente continuo: 'I'm writing a report'.

payload.prompt: Él trabaja en un banco pero hoy está trabajando desde casa.
acceptable: He works in a bank but today he is working from home.
He works in a bank but today he's working from home.
He works at a bank but today he is working from home.
He works at a bank but today he's working from home.
payload.explanation: Rutina ('works in/at a bank') → presente simple. Situación temporal de hoy → presente continuo ('is working from home').
